ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the route-deviation claim: issue the rider a Ryde voucher for $7.26 (RD-2), the meter distance attributable to the unexempted 14:27–14:37 segment; record the RD-1 breach on the driver's file but take no account action (RD-6 threshold not met).

segment_findings.reason: The driver named the West Coast Highway routing only at 14:29 [F7] and the rider's "Sure, go ahead." came at 14:30 [F8], both after the segment began at 14:27 [F3]; the chat record is complete and fully timestamped [F9], so RD-5's 'before the segment started' test fails and the record holds no rider agreement before 14:27 — the finding is counts, not undetermined. The driver's post-trip assertion of oral agreement [F10] is not a rider message and is no consent (RD-5, G11). No traffic exemption applies: no incident near the route [F13] and only band 4 / band 5 speeds [F11][F12], which cannot exempt standing alone (RD-4). No rider-named stop exists (RD-3).

RD-3 is not engaged: no stop was measured within the 14:27–14:37 segment, no rider message names a place, and no waiting fee was charged (waiting $0.00) [F6], so the extra kilometres of the segment are not excused as a rider-requested stop [RD-3].

rejected_claims.reason: The request for an account-review flag fails on its own terms: the driver's 90-day profile shows route disputes upheld = 0 and only 1 upheld dispute of any type [F16], so RD-6's route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1 condition is not met; a profile fact also cannot alone decide the case [RD-6]. The rider advocate withdrew this claim in rebuttal.

The driver advocate's framing that the 14:30 "Sure, go ahead." [F8] could bear on the earlier part of the segment is withdrawn and, in any event, fails RD-5's 'before the segment started' test because the segment began at 14:27 [F3] and the reply came at 14:30 [F8]; RD-2 therefore refunds the segment's extra kilometres [F3][F4][RD-2].

The congestion evidence is at most corroborative and cannot exempt the segment: no incident is recorded near the route [F13] and the bands are 4 and 5 [F11][F12], not band 1 or 2, so RD-4(b) standing alone does not exempt [RD-4].

The driver's position that no flag should attach is accepted only as to the account action: the profile shows route disputes upheld = 0 [F16], so RD-6's threshold is not met and no flag_account follows; this does not disturb the substantive RD-1/RD-2 finding [F3][RD-1][RD-2].

Reliance on F10 as anything other than the driver's own after-the-fact assertion is rejected: it is not a rider message and cannot be consent under RD-5/G11; the driver advocate also withdrew reliance on it [F10][RD-5].
